data.claim: Any run that invoked non-deterministic components—external tool calls, real-world I/O, unseeded randomness, or reads from mutable external state—must refuse resumption unconditionally. Only fully deterministic runs (pure computation over immutable inputs, all randomness seeded and recorded as events) are resumable. This is conservative: it refuses resumption even when a clean halt occurred, because the continuation after resumption may produce semantically different events than an uninterrupted run would have, and the append-only log cannot distinguish 'genuinely continued' from 'divergently restarted' events.
